messages.content:
In a group of 64 people, each person has a unique number written on their shirt, ranging from 1 to 64. They are standing in a circle, with the first person holding a ball. The ball is passed from person to person in the following pattern:
1. The ball is passed from the first person to the second person. 
2. The second person passes the ball to the fifth person. 
3. The fifth person passes the ball to the eleventh person. 
4. The eleventh person passes the ball to the twenty-third person. 
5. This pattern continues, with the ball being passed to the person whose position in the circle is the closest prime number greater than the previous position. For example, if the ball was just passed from the 23rd person, it would then be passed to the 29th person, the closest prime number greater than 23. If the ball was just passed from the 43rd person, it would be passed to the 47th person, the closest prime number greater than 43. 
The last person to receive the ball is declared the winner. What is the number on their shirt?

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

message.content:
**Answer – the winner’s shirt reads “61”.**

---

### How the game proceeds  

Let us write down what really happens when the ball keeps going to the **nearest prime number that comes after the current holder**.

| Current holder | Prime that is strictly larger |
|-----------------|--------------------------------|
| 1               | 2                              |
| 2               | 3                              |
| 3               | 5                              |
| 5               | 7                              |
| 7               | 11                             |
| 11              | 13                             |
| 13              | 17                             |
| 17              | 19                             |
| 19              | 23                             |
| 23              | 29                             |
| 29              | 31                             |
| 31              | 37                             |
| 37              | 41                             |
| 41              | 43                             |
| 43              | 47                             |
| 47              | 53                             |
| 53              | 59                             |
| 59              | 61                             |

When the ball reaches **61**, the very next prime would be **67**—but nobody wears a shirt numbered 67, because the shirts run only from 1 to 64.  
Therefore the chain stops here, and the last person to touch the ball is the wearer of shirt **61**.

---

### Quick sanity‑check  

If someone were to continue past 61, the next prime would be 67, which lies outside the set {1,…,64}. Hence 61 is the greatest possible “last” number obtainable by this procedure. All other candidates below 61 can be reached earlier in the chain, so 61 is uniquely determined as the winning shirt number.
